references.text: Bilhah is given to Rachel as her servant, which is relevant because Bilhah later bears children for Jacob on Rachel's behalf.
Rachel gives her servant Bilhah to Jacob as a wife so that she may have children through her. Bilhah bears Dan as the first son, and verse 7 describes the birth of the second child.
Rachel names the child Naphtali and explains the meaning of the name: 'With great wrestlings I have wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed.' This is the direct continuation of verse 7.
Summarizes Bilhah's sons Dan and Naphtali among Jacob's twelve sons, confirming her contribution to Jacob's descendants.
Lists Naphtali's sons and confirms that Dan and Naphtali were Bilhah's sons with Jacob, in connection with Jacob's family traveling to Egypt.
Connects the individual birth of Naphtali to the final counting of Bilhah's lineage in Egypt.
Parallel account of the rivalry between Leah and Rachel where God gives sons to both households.
Parallel in God's intervention to give sons to both Leah and Bilhah in the struggle for Jacob's affection.
